short: VCVTS's unit targets, speech-trained decoder and F0 predictor (M02, M03, M06) came early but are untested by ablation: standard. No WER, unlike its baselines: evaluation (M12) behind.
position: VCVTS [@wang2022vcvts] changes three components: lips predict the codebook indices of a voice-conversion content encoder (M02), that system is trained on speech alone and reused as the synthesizer (M03), and its decoder adds an F0 predictor (M06). Unit targets and the F0 predictor reach video-to-speech here earlier than in any other ledger study (Appendix), decoder transfer follows TaLNet [@zhang2021talnet], and all three became common from 2023 ([later]: [@choi2023intelligible; @kefalas2023large; @kim2025faces]); each rates standard because Table 1 compares whole systems and no ablation isolates any of them (§3). Evaluation (M12) is behind: intelligibility is claimed without any word error rate, although both baselines [@prajwal2020learning; @oneata2021speaker] and the best comparable earlier GRID study [@mira2021endtoend] score output with ASR. With Griffin-Lim on both sides, the GRID listener-test lead over Lip2Wav lies inside the 95% intervals (Table 1). Speaker control (M07) is the usual reference-audio embedding and degrades sharply on unseen GRID speakers.
